canonical_name: Radamsa 0.6 -- a general-purpose mutational fuzzer (Aki Helin, OUSPG), written in Owl Lisp
lineage: Black-box mutation fuzzing (Miller 1990 'fuzz'; Helin's Radamsa 2010-): take valid samples, apply a menu of structural mutations (byte flips, repeats, list/tree edits, number nudges) and emit adversarial inputs. Written in Owl Lisp (Helin's own purely functional Scheme dialect) and compiled to C -- a legacy-culture artifact as well as a pressure generator. PAIR: radamsa (pressure) <-> cJSON (the parser under attack).
build_system: make (fetches the Owl Lisp compiler ol at build time; recorded)
compiler_or_interpreter: gcc 12 (docker bookworm); ol (Owl Lisp) to regenerate radamsa.c
dependencies: Owl Lisp compiler ol 0.1.19 (companion artifact ol-0.1.19.c.gz, pinned; the Makefile would otherwise wget it)
upstream_docs: Miller, Fredriksen, So, An Empirical Study of the Reliability of UNIX Utilities, CACM 1990

human_capability_summary.built_to: manufacture inputs that are almost valid, in volume, to find where a parser breaks
human_capability_summary.pressure: the parser's assumptions; the human need to find crashes before attackers do
human_capability_summary.success_means: the emitted cases are diverse, reproducible under a seed, and reach deep parser states

human_environmental_pressure: adversarial input, the asymmetry between one parser and unbounded malformed input
human_failure_condition: mutations too shallow (all rejected at the first byte) or non-reproducible
behavioral_entry_point: change the seed and mutation menu (-m); pipe the cases into cjson-1.7.18's parser under ASan

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run radamsa-0.6
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: manufacture inputs that are almost valid, in volume, to find where a parser breaks
